summary: Implement ADR-021: per-ticket lifecycle chain + async organizer checkpoint + verify-lifecycle
description:
Implement the ticket lifecycle trail integrity scheme decided in ADR-021 (TKT-57). Until this lands, `lifecycle_events` is append-only by policy (the `lifecycle_events_immutable` trigger, which is DDL and removable) and NOT tamper-evident — and ADR-003 §Decision 2 makes redemption decisions from that trace, so it is a fraud surface, not just an audit gap.

ADR-021 decides the WHAT; this ticket owns the HOW. Read ADR-021 in full before planning — every clause below is load-bearing and several are deliberate divergences from the money journal that must not be 'fixed' back.

Scope:
- Per-ticket hash chain (ticket-local sequence, previous_hash, entry_hash) in a COMPANION integrity table; `lifecycle_events` is immutable and must not be rewritten. Lifecycle row + integrity row in one transaction; verifiers assert one-to-one coverage.
- Appends serialize on the ticket row `Redeem` already locks (postgres.go:182). NO organizer-wide lock, ever — that constraint is the whole reason ADR-021 rejected copying the money journal.
- Asynchronous per-organizer checkpoint: signed Merkle root over per-ticket heads CHANGED since the previous checkpoint (delta, not full scan), chained to it. Default interval 60s.
- Ed25519 under an `access-lifecycle/` key namespace, distinct key material from `access-qr/` (token.go:61-78 has the keyring idiom).
- Sign the HEAD, not every entry (ADR-021 §Decision 5).
- `Redeem` fails OPEN with a high-severity alarm on a chain that does not verify (ADR-021 §Decision 6).
- `access verify-lifecycle` subcommand, public keys only; wire into `scripts/smoke.sh` against populated AND deliberately corrupted data, mirroring what smoke.sh:78-105 already does for `verify-journal`.
- Versioned, domain-separated canonical form; no PII, no `guest_order_ref`; pinned by golden tests.
- Resumable startup backfill, bounded and fail-fast per ADR-008; adopts existing history as baseline.
- Migrations: plain `CREATE INDEX`, never CONCURRENTLY (ADR-020 — migrations run at startup).

Test seam (verified to exist at HEAD): `services/access/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go` — already provisions an isolated PostgreSQL schema, upgrades 0001→0002, preserves issued/delivered history, redeems, and asserts the immutability trigger rejects an UPDATE. Extend it; next migration is 0003.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Spun out of **TKT-57**, which decided this ([ADR-021](../../docs/adr/ADR-021-ticket-lifecycle-trail-integrity.md)) and deliberately shipped decision-only. TKT-57 is closed by the ADR; this ticket is the one that actually closes the gap.

**Three things the TKT-57 plan gate flagged that this ticket inherits as obligations, not suggestions:**

1. **Checkpoint freshness must be monitored.** The async checkpoint is a job that can silently stop, and if it does, the trail degrades to per-ticket-only — reopening the exact fraud ADR-021 closes, *with no symptom at the gate*. A stale checkpoint is an integrity alarm. This is the single biggest risk in the design.
2. **The fail-open alarm must actually route somewhere.** ADR-021 §Decision 6 admits on a bad chain and alarms. That is only safe *because* the alarm is load-bearing — an unmonitored alarm turns the clause into a silent bypass. Own the routing, don't assume it.
3. **The checkpoint interval IS the fraud window.** A head rolled back before any checkpoint included it is undetectable. 60s is the default; justify it, don't inherit it.

**Two items from the TKT-57 draft are CONTESTED, not approved** — the Codex plan draft proposed them and the plan review pushed back. Justify them on their own merits here or drop them:

- Extracting a shared `services/access/internal/signing` package is **speculative until there is a second consumer**. Adding lifecycle key loading beside the QR loader in `cmd/access/main.go` may be the entire change.
- The `internal/ticket/token.go` refactor is scope this ticket must earn. The QR signer works; do not churn it to make the new code look symmetric.

**Also worth doing while here** (found during TKT-57 verification, not required by ADR-021): `scripts/smoke.sh:56` runs the access store smoke suite under `-run TestRedeemedLifecycleMigrationPreservesHistory`. That allowlist means a newly added smoke test silently never runs while the gate stays green. Lines 48 and 59 of the same file already call this out as a defect that stranded tests twice — access is the last block still carrying one. Drop the filter.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Amended after the TKT-57 Codex adversarial review (PR #49).** ADR-021 changed materially; three items below are now **prerequisites, not polish**. Re-read ADR-021 §Decision 2, §Decision 5 and §Decision 6 — the earlier draft of each overclaimed and was corrected.

1. **The checkpoint signer must refuse to launder a rollback.** It must not extend a chain whose head has regressed relative to the last root it observed — it must refuse and escalate. **That last-observed root has to live somewhere the database adversary does not control**, or the check is circular and buys nothing. Choosing where is this ticket's call and it is load-bearing: without it, an attacker truncates the checkpoint suffix and the signer re-blesses the rolled-back state under a fresh valid signature.

2. **Checkpoint freshness monitoring IS the detection mechanism** for targeted rollback — not a nice-to-have. ADR-021 §Decision 2 is explicit that the checkpoint does *not* make rollback cryptographically detectable; staleness is the only signal. Unmonitored, the checkpoint buys attacker cost and nothing else.

3. **Fail-open needs its bounds implemented, or it is a bypass.** ADR-021 §Decision 6 now mandates: **quarantine** (a ticket failing verification is admitted once, then every later scan is denied and escalated), **threshold escalation** (integrity failures above a configured rate flip the organizer into operator-controlled mode), and **alarm routing with response SLOs**. An unmonitored deployment must not run fail-open. Fail-open means a *crude* chain corruption also admits — the attacker needs no finesse.

4. **Epoch signatures at rotation.** Head-only signing means a compromised *current* key can rewrite a ticket's whole history. On each rotation the outgoing key signs the head as it stands and that signature is retained, so a later compromise cannot rewrite pre-rotation history. The head signature binds ticket identity, ticket-local sequence, canonical version and key id — **not the head hash alone**.

Everything in the original description still applies.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Amended again after the SECOND Codex adversarial pass (PR #49).** The first amendment above is now partly wrong — read this one instead where they disagree.

**The root cause, which supersedes the four separate items above:** every control I listed stores its state **in the Access database — the very database the adversary is defined as owning**. Quarantine rows, threshold counters, retained epoch signatures, the signer's last-observed root: all deletable or resettable by the same attacker who caused the failure. ADR-021 now leads with **§The trust boundary** saying exactly this. Do not add a control to this ticket whose evidence lives in Access and call it containment.

What that changes for this ticket:

1. **The checkpoint buys no detection today. It is scaffolding for TKT-11** — one anchorable root per interval instead of one per ticket head. Build it for that reason. Do not describe it in code comments, dashboards or metrics as rollback protection.
2. **The signer's regression check needs a durable, attacker-independent home, or it does not exist.** ADR-021 §Decision 2 requires this ticket to either *specify that location* or *state plainly that no tripwire exists until TKT-11*. Leaving it ambiguous is what made two drafts of the ADR wrong — do not inherit the ambiguity.
3. **Quarantine + threshold escalation are still worth building — but they bound OUR BUGS, not attackers.** A canonicalization bug or botched rotation corrupting many chains at once is the case they contain. Against a database-write adversary, fail-open is unbounded, full stop. Say so wherever this surfaces to an operator.
4. **Epoch signatures are partial.** They stop *forgery* under a retired key, not *deletion* of the epoch row. Real containment needs an externally retained rotation manifest binding every applicable ticket to its epoch head (TKT-11's domain). Implement epoch signatures, but do not claim they contain a current-key compromise.

**New coupling worth surfacing to whoever plans TKT-11:** that ticket now owns strictly more than "fiscal archive". It owns the trust domain that the ticket lifecycle trail's rollback protection, signer continuity, quarantine integrity and epoch manifests all depend on. That dependency did not exist before ADR-021 and should be on TKT-11's radar before it is planned.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Context-mémo refreshed — ADR-022 landed hours after ADR-021 and moved the ground under §Decision 9.**

Migrations no longer run at service startup ([ADR-022](../../docs/adr/ADR-022-out-of-band-service-migrations.md), TKT-66, merged #50). ADR-021 §Decision 9 said the backfill runs *"at startup, before listening, per ADR-008"*. **That premise is gone**, and I have amended the ADR rather than leave this ticket to discover it at drafting time.

**The part that is a real design problem, not a word swap:** the backfill now runs in the one-shot `access-migrate` job, and ADR-008's surviving **30-second fail-fast deadline** now bounds *that job* — which the service `depends_on` with `service_completed_successfully`. This backfill is **not DDL**: it Ed25519-signs every existing `lifecycle_events` row, so its cost scales with history. **Blow the deadline and the migrate job fails, so Access never starts.** Deciding whether it fits — or needs its own resumable job outside the migrate deadline — is this ticket's call, and it is now flagged in `readiness.uncertainties`.

**Also worth noticing:** this mémo was baked ~1 hour before it went stale. The mémo exists so the planner does not have to re-derive decision history — but a mémo is a *snapshot*, and a fast-moving registry outruns it. Re-validate `governingAdrs` against `docs/adr/` at claim time; do not trust `capturedAt` alone.

objective.note: Make the ticket lifecycle trail tamper-evident against modification and insertion, per ADR-021.

scope.note: IN: per-ticket chain + companion integrity table, async organizer checkpoint, Ed25519 under access-lifecycle/, epoch signatures at rotation, fail-open + quarantine/threshold, verify-lifecycle + smoke wiring, resumable startup backfill. OUT: TKT-11's external anchor; the shared internal/signing extraction and token.go refactor are CONTESTED (see comments) and must be justified or dropped.

uncertainties.note: Identified, resolved at the plan gate. (1) Where the checkpoint signer's last-observed root lives so a DB-write adversary cannot reach it (ADR-021 §D2) — not blocking, the ADR allows stating plainly that no tripwire exists until TKT-11. (2) NEW, via ADR-022: the backfill now runs in the one-shot migrate job under ADR-008's 30s fail-fast deadline, and it Ed25519-signs every existing lifecycle row — so it may not fit, and the service `depends_on` that job completing. Decide whether it fits or needs its own resumable job outside the deadline. (3) Whether the contested internal/signing extraction earns its keep.

dependencies.note: ADR-021 decided (TKT-57, merged #49). Nothing blocks implementation. TKT-11 owns the external anchor and is NOT required for this to ship. See the one-redemption-cap decision ticket: deciding it after this means re-backfilling a signed trail.

approach.note: ADR-021 is the spec; read §The trust boundary first. Companion integrity table (never rewrite lifecycle_events), appends on the ticket row Redeem already locks, plain CREATE INDEX (ADR-020), startup backfill (ADR-008).

first_slice.note: Migration 0003 + chain append/verify on the existing issued/delivered/redeemed path, green through the existing smoke seam. Checkpoint job and verify-lifecycle follow within the ticket.

success.note: COS in the description; ADR-021's DoD is authoritative. Gate: make check, incl. verify-lifecycle against deliberately corrupted Access data mirroring smoke.sh:78-105.

context_memo.note: Baked below at shaping (TKT-57 retro R2: the planner reads code, not decision history).

governingAdrs.rule: THE spec for this ticket. Deliberate divergences from the money journal (Ed25519 not HMAC; sign the head not every entry; per-ticket not per-organizer) must NOT be 'fixed' back. §The trust boundary governs every claim.
§D7 — coordinated rollback is deferred to TKT-11. Do not claim to close it; do not re-solve it here.
§D2 trace-derived redemption (why this matters); §D3 no PII and no guest_order_ref in the canonical form; §D4's NF525 no-schema-change constraint is money-specific and does NOT bind this trail.
One DB per service. Chain, heads, checkpoints, signing, verification all live inside Access. Link to orders/journal by identifier only — no cross-DB FK, no shared chain.
Access already owns Ed25519 QR signing with an injected seed + kid (token.go:61-78, the access-qr/ namespace convention). Reuse the idiom, separate the key material.
Contention model: lock the ticket, never the organizer. The reason ADR-021 rejected the money journal's granularity.

SUPERSEDES ADR-008 ON PLACEMENT. Migrations run OUT-OF-BAND as a one-shot `<service>-migrate` Compose job (`migrate` subcommand); the server path never migrates and the service `depends_on` the job with `service_completed_successfully`. There is no 'before listening' any more. Single-invoker serialization is the invariant — advisory locking is deliberately deferred, and anything that could launch two migrate jobs per service must adopt it first.

SUPERSEDED ON PLACEMENT by ADR-022 — do NOT read it as 'migrations run at startup'. What still stands and still binds: goose v3 as a library, migrations embedded via embed.FS, per-service schema ownership, seed data as ordinary migrations, and FAIL-FAST UNDER A 30-SECOND DEADLINE.

Plain CREATE INDEX, never CONCURRENTLY — still. ADR-022 satisfied precondition (1) (migrations left startup), but the preconditions are CONJUNCTIVE and (2)/(3) remain false, so the decision is unchanged. TKT-66 amended ADR-020 to say exactly this; the premise that decoupling re-opens CIC was checked and rejected at its plan gate.

reference.summary: TKT-57 — the decision, its two adversarial review passes and six confirmed findings
Test seam, verified at HEAD: upgrades 0001→0002, preserves history, redeems, asserts the immutability trigger
Money-journal reference implementation: chain, sign, verify-journal + smoke corruption harness
ADR-021 §Decision 9 was AMENDED for ADR-022 — the backfill moved to the migrate job and now sits under a 30s job deadline it may not fit. Read the amendment, not the original clause.
